statement: The graph of the linear function $h$ in the $xy$-plane passes through the point $(4, 10)$ and has an $x$-intercept of $9$. What is the value of $h(0)$?

choices.misconception: I found the slope $-2$ but moved the wrong way: going from $x = 4$ to $x = 0$ I subtracted 8 instead of adding it, so I got $10 - 8 = 2$.
I thought the $y$-intercept had to equal the $x$-intercept, so I gave $h(0) = 9$.
I found the slope as run over rise, $\dfrac{5}{-10} = -\dfrac{1}{2}$, so going back 4 units I added only 2 and got $h(0) = 12$.

hints: An $x$-intercept of $9$ means the graph passes through $(9, 0)$.
Find the slope from $(4, 10)$ and $(9, 0)$, then move from $x = 4$ to $x = 0$.
The slope is $\dfrac{0 - 10}{9 - 4} = -2$. Going left 4 units, the line rises $2 \times 4 = 8$.

solutions.reliable: The graph passes through $(4, 10)$ and $(9, 0)$, so the slope is $\dfrac{0 - 10}{9 - 4} = -2$ and $h(x) = -2x + b$. From $h(9) = 0$, $b = 18$, so $h(0) = 18$. Check: $h(4) = -8 + 18 = 10$.
